subject: Proposed latency/uptime exhibit and telemetry commitments for Clearway Health
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@clearwayhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@clearwayhealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA exhibit + telemetry retention for Clearway deal CLW-2029-041

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement wants us to lock in availability and latency commitments in the Order Form before we route to legal. Two specific asks from our side: 

1) A latency commitment for API P95 response time for inference across our production workload (we're primarily leveraging chat + embeddings). We need a P95 <= 250ms for text-generation requests up to 512 tokens; if that target is missed in a monthly window, we want a credit schedule (tiered) rather than a single binary credit.

2) Telemetry & evidence: our security/compliance team requires a telemetry retention statement (metrics, per-route latency, token counts) and a path for audit evidence (past 90 days) plus an escalation contact for incidents. Can you confirm what you can include as an exhibit vs. what requires an SLA exception?

We can share a redline of the Order Form language if helpful. Targeting execs signoff by end of next week.

Appreciate it —
Maria Lopez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Clearway Health

Attachment: clearway_requirements_030929.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@clearwayhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA exhibit + telemetry retention for Clearway deal CLW-2029-041

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can propose an SLA Exhibit that covers a tiered credit schedule for P95 latency breaches and a separate availability uptime target. A few notes up front so we align expectations:

- Latency: We can commit to P95 <= 250ms for generation requests up to 512 tokens on our Dedicated tier (which Clearway has committed to), provided the traffic distribution remains within the profiles shared during onboarding. For hosted/shared capacity there are different targets.
- Tiered credits: propose three tiers (minor, material, severe) based on percentage of minutes missed in a monthly window. We'll include concrete credit percentages in the exhibit.
- Telemetry: we can provide per-route latency/time-series, token counts, and error traces for 90 days in the Console. For longer-term evidence (audit packages), our Evidence team can export a signed packet (metrics + runbook + incident timeline) for the prior 90 days on request.

Looping in Kimberly for order form/legal touchpoints and Karthik for operational evidence/telemetry scope below.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We share a redlined SLA Exhibit (I attach a draft).
2) If Clearway is comfortable, we route the exhibit with the Order Form for a single DocuSign envelope.
3) For any availability deviations that exceed the proposed thresholds, we can offer a short-term uplift of support (phone-oncall) as part of the remediation; we'll note that in the exhibit.

I'll wait for the redline but attached is our draft exhibit and the telemetry evidence matrix for your review.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts (Sales)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Exhibit_Clearway_redlines.docx, Telemetry_Evidence_Matrix.xlsx

Markus / Karthik —

Quick internal read and suggested edits before we send to Maria: 

- Redline the credit schedule to be caps-only (we should limit max monthly credit to 50% of the monthly invoice) and add an explicit exclusion for latency degradation caused by customer-side request patterns that exceed the agreed traffic profile.
- For telemetry retention, propose guaranteeing 90 days of console metrics, with an optional 6- or 12-month archive available as a billable add-on (we shouldn't commit to indefinite retention by default).
- Add an operational evidence SLA path: within 10 business days we'll provide an evidence packet when requested for an availability incident. For repeated evidence requests we should require an AD-hoc Statement of Work.

Karthik — can you confirm the P95 measurement approach (route-level vs global) and whether we can reasonably guarantee 250ms P95 in our Dedicated configs for the Clearway production traffic? If not, propose alternate language.

If you both approve, I'll incorporate these edits into the attached doc and we can route to Maria with a DocuSign envelope and the suggested exhibit.

Kimberly Park
VP, Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Markus —

Quick technical read:

- Measurement: we should measure P95 at the route level (per-API key + route) over 1-minute rolling windows and report aggregated daily/monthly P95 as the metric for the exhibit. That aligns with our Console metrics and reduces disputes.
- Feasibility: for Dedicated capacity with the expected token lengths and concurrency profile you shared, 250ms P95 is feasible 95% of months. However, to be safe I propose we include a conditional clause: the latency commitment applies when average CPU/GPU utilization for the serving pool is < 70% and when request size distribution remains within the documented profile. If Clearway expects larger seasonal bursts we should either passivate them through autoscale or agree to different thresholds.
- Credits: I agree with Kimberly on a capped schedule. Also recommend including a remediation credit (partial credit + free professional services hours for documented outages > 72 hours) for major incidents.

I'll add a short appendix describing the measurement method and the evidence exports we can produce (console CSV + signed telemetry packet).

I'll merge these changes into the exhibit and send back for legal redline.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Service Reliability
Redwood Inference

Maria —

Thanks for the patience while we incorporated feedback from Legal and Reliability. Attached are: (1) a redlined SLA Exhibit with the tiered credit schedule and measurement appendix, (2) the updated Order Form (Clearway_OrderForm_v2.pdf) and (3) the telemetry evidence matrix. Key points: 

- Latency commitment (P95 <= 250ms) applies to production routes under the Dedicated deployment and when the serving pool utilization is < 70%. We measure P95 per-route (API key + route) on 1-minute rolling windows and report aggregated monthly P95.
- Credit schedule: three tiers (minor/material/severe); monthly credit capped at 50% of monthly invoice. Credits are calculated as percentage of monthly invoice and applied as billing credit in the subsequent invoice.
- Telemetry: 90-day console retention guaranteed; 6/12 month archive available as paid add-on. Evidence packet provided within 10 business days of a formal request for an availability incident.
- Oncall uplift: for breaches in the material/severe tiers we include a 30-day phone escalation and a post-incident evidence package.

If that language looks good, we'll send this as a DocuSign envelope (two recipients: Maria + Clearway legal) and route a copy to your procurement team. DocuSign link below.
